name: pmc_before_kernel_rewrite
description: Before rewriting a kernel from Triton/CK to HIP for 'more speed', profile the baseline with PMC counters. If it is memory-bound (SQ_WAIT_INST_LDS/SQ_INSTS_LDS >> 0.5 OR the kernel is already near HBM bandwidth), the waitcnt-reduction lever the HIP path offers does NOT move wall-clock — you will spend days getting parity.
preconditions: Considering a HIP port of a Triton / CK / hipBLASLt kernel
Access to rocprofv3 and the baseline kernel running on the target shape
steps: Run PMC: SQ_INSTS_LDS, SQ_WAIT_INST_LDS, SQ_WAIT_ANY, MfmaUtil, VALUUtilization, GRBM_GUI_ACTIVE
Compute LDS stall ratio = SQ_WAIT_INST_LDS / SQ_INSTS_LDS
- LDS stall ratio > 0.5 AND MfmaUtil < 40% → compute-bound with LDS-waitcnt pathology → HIP port wins (Triton's tl.dot_scaled pattern on gfx950)
- LDS stall ratio > 0.5 AND MfmaUtil > 60% → compute-bound near ceiling → HIP port gives marginal 1.1-1.2×
- Stall_ratio any AND kernel at >70% HBM BW peak → memory-bound → HIP port matches, does not beat
- Stall ratio ~0.1, VALUUtilization > 95%, MfmaUtil < 50% → latency-hiding limited (occupancy) → HIP port needs occupancy-lifting lever (shrink LDS/VGPR), not waitcnt
Make ship/no-ship decision BEFORE writing kernel code
expected_impact: Saves 1-2 weeks of kernel engineering on memory-bound ports. Experience: HIP fwd grouped GEMM won 1.13× Triton (compute-bound, waitcnt lever live); HIP wgrad was projected 1.0× (memory-bound, no lever) and deferred without wasted work.
decision_rules: Triton tl.dot_scaled on gfx950 is the ONE clear case where a HIP port guaranteed wins — its MLIR lowering has ~14 s_waitcnt/cluster vs HIP ~0.05/MFMA. See knowledge_base/triton/tl_dot_scaled_gfx950.md.
Memory-bound kernels (wgrad, long-K reductions, any kernel where AI < compute/BW balance point) give parity at best.
When in doubt, measure the baseline's AMDGCN s_waitcnt count per MFMA as a quick compute-side sanity check.
